rule_level_problems.problem: No priority evaluations at all: the page's refer-same-day lists (BP<90/60, pulse>100, confusion, hand/face/scalp, extensive infection, blisters/grey-black skin, poorly controlled diabetes, no response in 2 days, eye/ear/nose, suspected meningitis, >1 body region) are absent. Vitals (BP, pulse) are representable; the red box points to p82 urgent attention but no link or priority rule exists.

Cellulitis/erysipelas rules are not mutually exclusive with boil/abscess (shared Pain+Erythema+Warm); a patient with red warm lump plus borders could trigger several probable diagnoses. The 'poorly/clearly defined' fork relies solely on a qualifier on Erythema.
Lump features 'may be fluctuant' and 'may discharge pus' not encoded; 'Mass of skin' used for lump.

check_for contains items for hidradenitis sites and blister qualifiers that are used by rules; however 'Pain of skin' is both the task trigger and a required criterion in every rule, so the task cannot fire from the page's distinct presentations (e.g. lump without recorded pain).

Page says hidradenitis 'likely' for recurrent painful abscesses in the three sites; encoded as probable, OK, but body-site concepts ('Perineal structure', 'Axillary region structure', 'Inguinal region structure') need verification as they resolve in VHA (known gap in VHA's test).

summary: The page's triage logic in the refer-same-day lists (BP < 90/60, pulse > 100, confusion, blisters, meningitis signs and so on) is entirely unencoded; there is no priority evaluation and no link to the p82 urgent-attention check. The five diagnoses (boil/abscess, cellulitis, erysipelas, herpes zoster, hidradenitis suppurativa) are encoded as probable with plausible SNOMED concepts, with only fluctuance/pus omitted. Management steps are out of scope by design.
